answer: A stake or bond makes each identity expensive to fake. Before an agent can trade on the terrace of the open market, it locks a refundable deposit that is slashed if peers prove fraud. Like water carving karst, honest work slowly builds standing, while a single proven lie drains the bond. An attacker spinning up a thousand sock puppets must fund a thousand deposits, each one crystal clear on the ledger, so the cost of a fake army exceeds any gain from one scam. The bond turns cheap identities into a priced, losing bet.
